subject: Clarify geo pinning and transient cross-hop processing for MedSys (DPA addendum)
messages:
From: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@medsys.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Karim Haddad <k.haddad@medsys.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0400
Subject: Initial: geo controls, telemetry, and DPA addendum questions

Connor —

Thanks for taking this. We're working through the DPA review and have a couple of practical asks before we can move to legal review:

- Can Redwood commit to keeping customer data for MedSys instances pinned to EU datacenters for inference and storage by default?
- We understand there may be temporary cross-region processing for ops or caching. What is the maximum transient window you allow (hours/days) and how is it logged?
- Where does operational telemetry and usage metadata traverse? Are any telemetry sinks routed through the US or APAC?
- Please attach your current subprocessor roster, and a short description of any ephemeral caches (KV caches, prefetch buffers) that might leave the EU boundary.

I'm attaching our question spreadsheet. If we can get a short written statement for the DPA addendum (Annex) covering pinning, transient window, logging/audit trail, and KMS options, that will speed legal review.

Appreciate a concise answer so we can align with our security team.

Cheers,
Alice
Alice Monroe
Director, Cloud Security
MedSys Health

Attachment: MedSys-DPA-questions.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@medsys.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Apr 2027 11:12:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Initial: geo controls, telemetry, and DPA addendum questions

Alice —

Thanks for the clear list. High level answers below; I'm attaching a short playbook that maps our operational controls to the DPA clauses you referenced. Happy to follow up with a short call.

1) EU pinning: yes — by default we will serve and store customer data in the pinned region (EU) when a customer elects region pinning. This applies to model inputs, outputs, and persistent logs tied to requests.

2) Transient cross-hop windows: we permit transient cross-region processing only for specific operational reasons (replication backfill, emergency failover, metric aggregation) and only under the transient window documented in your SLA. Typical transient windows we provide as options are: 0 hours (strict pinning), up to 72 hours for controlled failover, or a consented window up to 7 days for archival backfills. Every transient event is written to an audit log with start/end timestamps and reason codes.

3) Telemetry and metadata: application-level telemetry (token counts, latency histograms) is aggregated and can be configured to remain within the pinned region. Platform health telemetry (host metrics, crash dumps) may be replicated to our centralized ops region for safety monitoring; we can route those through EU-only telemetry collectors on request or provide filtered views.

4) Ephemeral caches: our serving runtime uses short-lived KV caches on GPU hosts. For pinned deployments these caches are instantiated in-host within the same region; they are ephemeral and evicted regularly. We do not write KV cache contents to cross-region persistent stores.

5) KMS and keys: we offer customer-managed keys (bring-your-own KMS) for enterprise plans; keys can be provisioned in customer EU-managed KMS to avoid US-based key escrow.

Next steps: Lauren (legal) has a DPA addendum draft she can circulate. Grace (ops) can provide a network flow/telemetry diagram and confirm exact endpoints for our EU collectors. I've attached our region failover playbook.

Connor
Connor O'Brien
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-region-failover-playbook.pdf (pdf)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@medsys.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 09:37:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Initial: geo controls, telemetry, and DPA addendum questions

Alice / Connor —

Looping in legal. Quick clarifications and a proposed mechanism we typically use for customers with strong residency requirements:

- DPA addendum: we can add an Annex specifying region pinning with a transient-processing clause. Wording we propose: 'Redwood will store and process Customer Data within the designated region. Transient cross-region processing may occur for limited operational reasons, documented in Redwood logs. Transient processing duration will not exceed the Customer-selected window (0 hours / 72 hours / 7 days), except for emergency events subject to Customer notification).'

- Subprocessor roster: we will provide a current roster as a CSV. We will also include an attestation of subprocessor locations and whether they process customer data outside the EU.

- Audit and evidence: each transient cross-hop will generate an immutable audit entry (timestamp, initiating event, operator id, source/destination regions). We can provide these entries on request or stream to your SIEM via a push integration.

- KMS: for the strictest customers we recommend customer-managed keys housed in an EU KMS. That prevents Redwood from decrypting persistent artifacts outside your control.

I have started a DPA addendum draft and attached it along with the current subprocessor roster. If MedSys can confirm the pinning option you prefer (strict 0-hour vs 72-hour vs 7-day), we will produce the Annex and a redline-friendly doc.

If useful, Grace can produce a concise network flow diagram showing where ephemeral caches live and where telemetry flows.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: DPA-addendum-draft.docx (docx); subprocessor-roster.csv (csv)

From: Karim Haddad <k.haddad@medsys.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Monroe <alice.monroe@medsys.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Apr 2027 15:14:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Initial: geo controls, telemetry, and DPA addendum questions

Thanks for the quick responses. A few targeted asks so legal and architecture can move fast:

- Can you produce a one-page network flow diagram that shows: ingress points, where KV caches are instantiated, replication paths during a failover, and where telemetry collectors are located? Preferably PNG or PDF.
- Please confirm whether any ephemeral caches are ever written to durable storage outside the EU under normal operations. If yes, what are the conditions and retention rules?
- For the 72-hour option: can you confirm whether the audit entries will include operator id and full timestamps and whether MedSys can receive a daily digest?

If you can send the network diagram and a redlineable Annex by EOD Monday we will aim to push back to procurement next week. Also open to a 30-minute call early next week to walk through the playbook.

Regards,
Karim Haddad
Senior Counsel, MedSys Health

Attachment: network-flow-diagram-request.pdf (pdf)
